The thermometer that always says twenty

A day spent being certain, and wrong, about six different things. Every one of them had the same cause.

01 · the broken instrument

A tool that gives one answer is not measuring

Put it in ice, it reads twenty. Put it in the oven, it reads twenty. It never knew anything.

02 · what i actually did

I read the old copy instead of asking

To check whether work was saved, I read a list on my desk. I never asked the place it is saved.

03 · the expensive part

The wrong fix looked obvious to two of us

The error hinted at a broken machine. Two assistants, hours apart, reached for the same big lever.

04 · the quiet one

An empty box, stamped as delivered

A step was blocked, wrote nothing, and still printed success. Nothing shipped. Everything said shipped.

05 · the whole fix

Ask what it says when the answer is no

Before trusting a check, run it where the problem is absent. If nothing changes, it proved nothing.

So what?

Being wrong is cheap and normal. Being wrong while holding a tool that cannot disagree with you is what turns a small mistake into a confident one, and confident mistakes are the ones that get acted on.
